prerequisites: Cross-material knowledge of the structure of materials and their influence through processing. Influence of composition, manufacturing processes, and further processing on the property profiles of engineering materials.
Successful completion of StEOP (Study Induction and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the necessary knowledge to influence material properties through technological processes, such as heat treatment and thermo-mechanical treatment.
Know the basic manufacturing processes for metallic alloys, such as casting, rolling, or drawing/cold forming.
Gain practical experience in the application-oriented use of what has been learned.
Be able to independently develop an understanding of material-relevant issues in engineering sciences.
To appropriately apply technological processes and thermo-mechanical treatments for the targeted influencing of material properties.
To precisely describe basic manufacturing processes for metallic alloys.
To independently and methodically address application-oriented material-relevant issues in engineering sciences.
To clearly explain the formation and significance of the microstructure of materials for material application.
To structuredly present material science processes in thermal and mechanical material processing.
To clearly present process chains of typical manufacturing methods from raw material extraction to the setting of the mechanical-technological properties of the end product.
To systematically categorize typical structural materials and material groups with their areas of application.
To professionally perform relevant material testing procedures (e.g., CCT/Jominy, DMA, DSC, ceramic bending test).
To precisely describe the fundamentals and processes of raw material extraction.
To clearly formulate material testing protocols and measurement results.
To structuredly work on calculation examples and theoretical questions in written and oral examinations, both independently and in partner and group work.
To systematically examine measurement data, protocols, and test results for plausibility and consistency.
To compare alternatives of approaches in experimental execution and evaluation based on given criteria.
To concisely summarize content from lectures and illustrative examples.
To cooperatively and transparently formulate team roles, communication channels, and coordination rules in the lab and during exercises in communication with peers.
To purposefully plan work and learning processes with regard to time, resources, and quality.
To constructively discuss peer feedback on solutions and reports.

syllabus_topics: Formation and significance of the microstructure of materials for material application
Material science processes in material processing (thermal, mechanical, etc.)
Typical manufacturing processes for structural materials from raw material extraction to the setting of the mechanical-technological properties of the end product
Typical constructive materials/material groups and their areas of application in engineering sciences
Materials testing: CCT/Jominy, microstructure of plastics (DMA, DSC+solidification), ceramic bending test
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical fundamentals and basic instruments
Illustration of application through engineering examples

assessment_methods.method: Written and/or oral examination with calculation examples and theoretical questions
Tests and protocols for the exercise parts

assessment_rules: Performance control can be carried out through written and/or oral examinations with calculation examples and theoretical questions, tests and protocols for the exercise parts, regular homework, and class performance. The exact examination modalities will be announced before the start of the semester.
